sections.h2: Which Hernando County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three elected offices share the work in Hernando County: the property appraiser values parcels and grants exemptions, the tax collector sends and collects the bills, and the clerk records deeds and runs tax deed auctions. Most sellers deal with all three.

The tax collector's mailing address is 20 N. Main Street, Room 112, Brooksville, FL 34601, and questions can go to tc@hernandocounty.us. The tax collector's own site says the appraiser handles homestead exemptions, assessed values and name or address changes for notices. The Hernando County Property Appraiser keeps offices in Brooksville and in Spring Hill, and publishes a tax estimator and a parcel search.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, parcel search, ownership changes on the roll.
  • Tax Collector: tax bills, payments, installment plan, certificate sale.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: recorded deeds and tax deed sales.

sections.h2: When is Hernando County property tax due?
sections.html:
Hernando County bills in November, and the last day to pay without penalty is March 31. Every unpaid account becomes delinquent on April 1.

The tax collector lists the early payment discounts as 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February, with nothing off in March. The office honors the postmark on current-year payments sent during a discount period. Online e-check payments are free for current and delinquent bills, while cards carry a $2.75 minimum or 2.5% processing fee that goes to a third-party vendor.

Tangible personal property tax, which covers furniture, fixtures and equipment in businesses and rental properties, arrives on the same bill and earns the same discounts. A $25,000 exemption is available to owners who file a return by April 1, so landlords selling a rental should ask whether such an account exists for the address.

sections.h2: How does the Hernando County installment plan work?
sections.html:
The plan splits the bill into four quarterly payments, and you can only pay each installment in its own month. Enrollment opens every November 1 and closes April 30, and it is confirmed once the first June payment is made.

A late installment has to be paid with the next one. An unpaid balance on April 1 is delinquent and no discount applies. Withdrawing means giving up the discounts the law provides. The statute behind the plan is section 197.222.

Outside the plan, partial payments on the current year are possible from November 1 through March 31. That route needs a signed application, forfeits all discounts and allows only five partial payments, with the balance due by March 31.

sections.h2: What homestead rules apply in Hernando County?
sections.html:
A Hernando County homestead exemption can lower the taxable value of a primary residence by up to $50,000. The owner must live in the home as a permanent resident on January 1 of the year of application.

The appraiser's page says it is taking applications for the 2027 tax year, with a March 1, 2027 deadline, and that later applications count for the 2028 tax year. Owners can apply in person, by mail or through an online portal. Statewide, the Save Our Homes cap limits yearly growth to the lower of 3 percent or the change in the Consumer Price Index, and the Florida Revenue chart shows a 2.7 percent cap for 2026.

On the bill, the tax collector combines all exemptions into one dollar figure under the word Exemption. When a property is sold, the appraiser removes the owner's exemption and cap starting the next year, so a buyer must apply to start fresh.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Hernando County property tax?
sections.html:
Delinquent Hernando County tax earns 3% interest from April 1, gets listed in a local newspaper, and picks up advertising and collection fees. The tax collector auctions tax certificates online through LienHub at the end of May, and the page mentions May 29 as the cutoff for payment before the sale.

  • Bidding starts at 18 percent interest and falls in steps toward 0.25 percent.
  • The winning bidder pays the taxes and holds a first lien on the parcel.
  • A homestead parcel with a taxable amount under $250.00, or one in litigation, is struck off to the county.
  • A certificate lives seven years unless bankruptcy interrupts it.
  • After two years the holder can apply for a tax deed, and the clerk may then auction the property.

Delinquent bills can be paid by any method, but a parcel in tax deed status needs certified funds. If no one bids at a deed sale, the land goes on a list of lands available for taxes, and the county has the first 90 days to buy it.

sections.h2: What should a Hernando County seller know before closing?
sections.html:
A seller in Hernando County clears the tax from the sale proceeds, and a recorded deed is what moves the bill to the buyer. After a completed deed is recorded with the Clerk of the Circuit Court, the appraiser changes the owner on the roll, and the tax collector's record follows after the next certified tax roll in October.

Florida's documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county except Miami-Dade, and any party to the deed can be held liable. Ask the title company how the closing statement will split the current year's bill between buyer and seller, and whether any tangible personal property account sits on the same bill.

Millage rates are set by each taxing authority, which in Hernando County includes the Board of County Commissioners, the City of Brooksville, the school district and the Southwest Florida Water Management District. The appraiser posts a millage report once rates are updated at final roll certification. For the rate on your parcel, check the TRIM notice mailed in August or ask the tax collector.

sections.h2: How can a Hernando County owner challenge a value?
sections.html:
File a petition with the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, which the appraiser mails in August. Petitions go to the Value Adjustment Board, using one of the DR-486 forms. A petition filed after the deadline on the notice is out of time, so mark the date when the envelope arrives.

A denial of a homestead exemption, classification or deferral follows a different clock: petition the board within 30 days after the denial letter was mailed. The board deals with value and exemptions, and tax rates are set elsewhere, at the budget hearings of the taxing authorities in September and October. Homeowners with a rental or an agricultural parcel can ask the appraiser's office, which lists agricultural classification, mobile home and tangible property pages on its site, whether a separate filing applies.

faqs.q: When does Hernando County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Bills are due by March 31 of the year after they are issued, and the tax collector adds 3% interest to delinquent amounts, along with advertising and collection fees.

faqs.q: What discount does Hernando County give for early payment?
faqs.a: The discount is 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. There is no discount in March, and the postmark decides the date for current-year payments.

faqs.q: Does Hernando County take credit cards for tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes, with a $2.75 minimum or 2.5% processing fee charged by a third-party vendor. E-checks are free online for current and delinquent bills, and tax deed payments need certified funds.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the Hernando County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Apply with the property appraiser in person, by mail or through its online portal. The deadline for the 2027 tax year is March 1, 2027, and you must live in the home as your permanent residence on January 1.

faqs.q: Who runs the Hernando County tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: The tax collector runs it online through LienHub at the end of May each year. Bidders register with LienHub, and parcels are auctioned one at a time in parcel number order.
